title: NRCH swimmers SIM replicates on seed 3: 6 tracks travel 5-15 body lengths, the reciprocal twin is static (max 0.3 BL)
summary: Fresh seed 3 (192^2, t=6000): the noisy uniform state is featureless until t~1050, then droplets nucleate as polar crescents with a psi crest at the front (t=1300) and settle into 4-12 swimming droplets. labkit: 7 long-lived tracks moved >= 1 BL, 6 of them >= 5 BL (15.1, 12.0, 10.4, 10.2, 7.3, 5.3), speeds 0.10-0.18. The reciprocal twin (Dt=+0.3, same seed) forms 20-71 static round droplets that coarsen: 0 tracks >= 1 BL, max 0.3 BL.

observations.S: rerun/sheet.png t=0-800: uniform plus noise over the whole domain; droplets appear at t~1050
observations.I: rerun/tracks.png: tracks #23, #46, #47 followed for 2000-3000 t as single droplets
observations.M: rerun/metrics.json motion_top: track 23 15.1 BL, track 2 12.0 BL, tracks 30/35 ~10 BL at 0.16-0.18 per time; recip/ 0 tracks >= 1 BL

controls_run.M: recip/ (reciprocal D12=D21=+0.3, seed 3): static coarsening droplets, max 0.3 BL

verdicts.limitation: Droplets deform strongly and collide often in a crowded field (occupancy 0.22), so shape is kept only between collisions (tracks.png #40 changes from crescent to three-lobed). The world reproduces a published result (Brauns-Marchetti 2024). I ran no sub-threshold twin, no dt or resolution check, and no Laplacian-only twin (the nonreciprocal coupling itself is linear cross-diffusion; the phase separation is fourth order).
